This is a bit long, but I want you to read it because it's all based on my own experience. At the time, there were only my sister and I as customers; the rest were staff. The doctors were all on their lunch break, probably around 1:00 PM to almost 2:00 PM.

Today, I took my sister in for a consultation about orthodontic treatment. When we first walked in, the staff at the counter were polite and the service was normal. Then they asked us, "What is your budget?"

This surprised me a little, because it was the first time I'd encountered a clinic asking about a budget before offering braces. So I honestly told them that I hadn't prepared a budget yet, as I intended to have the doctor examine my sister first to see what needed to be done, and then we would discuss the costs.

The staff informed us that the doctor was on lunch break and that we should wait for the doctor to come in to assess our sister's oral health before the costs could be determined. My sister and I waited as usual.

But while we were waiting, we suddenly heard someone shouting and yelling from inside the clinic. I overheard something like, "The customer didn't tell me their budget, so why didn't they ask? If the costs exceeded what they said, am I supposed to pay for it? They were just sitting there typing whatever they wanted without asking. Don't think that just because they moved there, I can't do anything!"

I don't know what exactly happened, and I'm not trying to judge the clinic's internal affairs, but as a customer sitting outside the clinic and hearing that, it was very upsetting and uncomfortable. My perception of the clinic was very negative.

I even called home to ask if we should change clinics because I was starting to feel uneasy. But I thought, since we're already here, let's give it a chance.

When the doctor came in, it was the first doctor, likely an orthodontist. They gave a consultation about braces and oral cleaning, and told us to wait for another doctor to do further examinations before they could finalize the total cost.

While my sister needed to use the restroom, I waited outside. A staff member approached us and started discussing the cost, asking what we were going to do. We explained that the doctor said to wait for all the examinations before finalizing the price; we just wanted to know the total so we could decide whether to get braces right away or just do the oral cleaning first.

But at that point, I felt a little pressured because the staff member kept trying to get us to confirm, and followed us from the restroom to the counter. I felt uncomfortable, so I asked to go make a phone call to my family, who were paying for the treatment.

When I finished the call and came back, I saw my sister was already in the examination room with the doctor, so I followed her in.

Then the doctor said they were going to fill my sister's front tooth right away.

I was very confused about this because we hadn't confirmed any treatment yet. So we quickly told the doctor that we wanted to know the total cost before deciding. The doctor agreed and continued the examination.

After that, a staff member came to inform us of the price, but it seemed like they couldn't quite explain the details. We asked several times until we understood, and at that point, we thought we would proceed with the treatment.

But after a while, they informed us that the price didn't include the cost of filling deep cavities or something like that. So we asked if they could please give us the total cost so we could decide at once.

The staff member turned to ask other people how much it cost, but no one answered, and then they went to gather everyone to check the price again.

At that time, the atmosphere seemed very chaotic. It seemed like there wasn't much coordination within the clinic. Combined with the incident of people shouting and arguing earlier, it made us feel very uncertain.

Ultimately, we decided not to proceed. Because if we felt so uncomfortable after just the first visit, and orthodontic treatment requires many more visits to the doctor, we thought that if we forced ourselves to go ahead, we would be anxious every time we had to come.

So we told the clinic, "Sorry, we'd like to cancel the treatment," and walked out.

But I would like to commend the small female staff member with glasses. She tried her best to serve us well and didn't speak rudely at all. It's just that it seemed like she didn't have all the information she received, so she couldn't answer many questions. We understood that.

After we walked out, my sister told me that while we were making a phone call... I overheard people talking in the room, implying that we were being too demanding. I didn't hear it myself, so I can't confirm this, but after hearing it from my colleague, I felt hurt. Throughout my time at the clinic, I tried to remain calm and only wanted to know the total cost before deciding on treatment.

Ultimately, what bothered me the most was being asked about the cost before even having a dental examination. I'm not sure if this is standard practice at orthodontic clinics, but from my perspective, the cost should depend on the patient's dental problems and treatment plan, not on their initial budget.

This is just my experience from the day I visited the clinic. I have no intention of attacking anyone; I just wanted to share my real experience in case it's helpful for those who are making a decision.
